Question: For every positive real number $x$, let $g(x)=\lim _{{r \rightarrow 0}}((x+1)^{{r+1}}-x^{{r+1}})^{{1/r}}$. What is the limit of $g(x)/x$ as $x$ goes to infinity?

Options: 
A. 2
B. Infinity
C. 3.1415926
D. 1
E. 0
F. 1.6180339
G. 1.4142135
H. 1.7320508
I. 2.7182818
J. 3.1415927

The function $g(x)$ can be evaluated by finding the derivative of the inner term at $r=0$. Specifically, $\lim_{r \to 0} ((x+1)^{r+1}-x^{r+1})^{1/r} = \exp\left( (x+1)\ln(x+1) - x\ln x \right) = (x+1)\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)^x$. Dividing by $x$ and taking the limit as $x \to \infty$, we obtain $\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{g(x)}{x} = \lim_{x \to \infty} \left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)^{x+1} = e$. Since $e \approx 2.7182818$, the correct option is I.
